ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 17603, as amended; AML/CFT regime and beneficial ownership data reporting to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit); Enforcement Decree of the same Act (Presidential Decree No. 33843, as amended); Act on the Real Name Financial Transactions and Maintenance of Secrecy (Act No. 18301, as amended); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 19384, as amended); Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 19823, as amended); Prohibition of Criminal Proceeds Act (Act No. 17899, as amended); FATF Recommendations (2012, as revised).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registration Matters of a Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registry Office / District Court of Registration (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Division)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille track for Hague member states: issue certified registration matters through the Internet Registration Office (iROSe), obtain the court registrar's seal/signature verification if required, and present to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for an Apostille. Consular track for non-member states: do not apostille; present the original certified registration record to the Embassy or Consulate of the destination state in Korea for consular legalization. These two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (equivalent: Certificate of Current Registration Matters)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registry Office / District Court of Registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states: obtain the certified current registration record from the court registry, have any registrar signature notarized if requested by the receiving party, then obtain a Korean MOFA Apostille. For non-Apostille states: submit the same original certificate to the destination country's consular post in the Republic of Korea for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative routes, not a sequential chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing the representative director and local formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa members' meeting / board of directors, with signatory identity notarized by a licensed Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: After execution, the document is notarized by a Korean notary. Apostille path: the notarized document is submitted to MOFA for an Apostille in a member state. Consular path: the notarized document is submitted to the Korean embassy or consulate of the destination state in Korea for consular legalization. Only one path applies; never add consular legalization after an Apostille or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jeonggwan) of the Yuhan Hoesa, certified true copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public for the original draft; Supreme Court Registry Office for the certified registered copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain a certified copy of the registered Articles or a notarized duplicate. For an Apostille member state: notary seal verification where applicable, then MOFA Apostille. For a non-member state: consular legalization by the destination state's consular officer in Korea. The Apostille Convention route and the consular legalization route are mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (post-formation bank KYC/UBO verification letter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank after the company account is opened and customer due diligence is completed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille track: bank officer's signature/seal is notarized by a Korean notary, then the notarized letter is apostilled by MOFA. Consular track: the notarized bank letter is consular-legalized by the destination state's Korean diplomatic or consular mission. Use only the track mandated by the destination jurisdiction; never combine Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign Investment Report Certificate or Notification Receipt under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (if foreign-owned)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: KOTRA Invest KOREA Center or the designated foreign exchange bank receiving the foreign investment report
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: the official KOTRA/bank certificate is notarized if required, then apostilled by MOFA. Consular route: the same certificate is legalized by the destination state's consulate or embassy located in Korea. For any single document, only one route may be used, based on the destination state's membership in the Hague Apostille Convention.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before accepting any formation instruction, counsel must run a 100 percent identity-match screen against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the United Kingdom Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation Consolidated List, and the Republic of Korea's domestic financial sanctions and foreign-exchange designations under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the AML/CFT Act. Screening must use fuzzy matching, Hangul/romanization and alias variants, date-of-birth validation, address and passport/nationality cross-checks, and adverse-media enrichment. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), including foreign and domestic PEPs, family members and close associates, must be escalated for enhanced due diligence requiring source-of-wealth evidence, organizational charts, independent negative-news review, and written sign-off by the AML/CFT compliance partner before incorporating.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Registry Office Internet Registration Office (iROSe) company name search portal (https://www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered company name must be stated in the Korean alphabet and must include the mandatory legal-form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' to identify a Korean limited liability company. The Korean registry applies a four-tier commercial naming convention: (i) a distinctive proprietary brand or word, (ii) an optional descriptive business element such as online cosmetics retail, (iii) the statutory entity-type suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa', and (iv) an optional parallel English or romanized trade name used commercially on invoices, websites, and payment rails. The parallel English trade name is not the registered corporate name and cannot replace the Hangul name for

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Articles 288-300 (incorporation), 292 (articles of incorporation), 317 (registration), 330 (capital), 340 (shares), 383-408 (board of directors), and 560-568 (limited liability company provisions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Korean Commercial Registration Court (상업등기소) under the Supreme Court of Korea, administered by the local district court registry where the registered office is located
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Certificate of Incorporation (법인등기부등)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - South Korea does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC). The capital must be fully subscribed and paid in at incorporation, and the amount must be declared in the Articles of Incorporation. No escrow account or blocked capital requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (Yuhan Hoesa) HELD ON [DATE] AT [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS]

WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under the Commercial Act of South Korea (the 'Act') and has adopted its Articles of Incorporation on [DATE];

WHEREAS, the initial subscribers have subscribed to the entire authorized share capital of the Company, and the capital has been fully paid in as required by law;

WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is authorized to take all necessary actions to commence business operations and to comply with all applicable legal and regulatory requirements;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: The Board hereby confirms the subscription and allotment of the entire issued share capital of the Company, consisting of [NUMBER] shares of [PAR VALUE] Korean Won each, to the subscribers as set forth in the subscription list. The Board acknowledges that the full consideration for such shares has been received in cash or in kind as per the subscription agreements, and that the capital is fully paid up.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, jointly or severally, to open and maintain bank accounts in the name of the Company with any licensed commercial bank in South Korea. Such officers are authorized to execute all banking documents, sign checks, and issue payment instructions, subject to the internal control policies of the Company. The Board further authorizes the establishment of online banking facilities and the appointment of authorized signatories for all banking transactions.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [FULL ADDRESS], which shall be the legal seat of the Company for all statutory and administrative purposes. The Board directs the Company Secretary to file the registered office address with the Commercial Registration Court and to notify all relevant government agencies, including the National Tax Service and the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, of the registered office details.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board appoints the following officers to serve in the capacities indicated, effective immediately:
   - [NAME] as Chief Executive Officer (CEO), with full authority to manage the day-to-day operations of the Company and to represent the Company in all business matters.
   - [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer (CFO), with authority over financial management, accounting, and tax compliance.
   - [NAME] as Company Secretary, responsible for corporate governance, statutory filings, and maintenance of corporate records.
   - [NAME] as Compliance Officer, responsible for ensuring compliance with all applicable laws, including the Cosmetics Act and consumer protection regulations.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the CEO and CFO to execute all necessary documents, contracts, and filings required to commence business operations, including but not limited to business registration, tax registration, and any industry-specific licenses or notifications. The Board further authorizes the engagement of legal counsel and professional advisors as deemed necessary.

6. EFFECTIVE DATE: This resolution is effective as of the date of this meeting and shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting and filed with the Company's corporate records.

ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY by the Board of Directors on the date first written above.

[Signature of Chairperson]
[Signature of Secretary]

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Commercial Registration Court (상업등기소) – online via the Supreme Court's e-Registration system (인터넷등기소)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the e-Registration portal to ensure the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing registered entities. Reserve the name by filing an application with the court, which is valid for 6 months. Simultaneously, verify that the proposed business scope (online retail of cosmetics) does not require any special pre-approval beyond standard registration. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the company name, purpose, registered office address, share capital, and number of shares. All initial subscribers must sign the articles, and if any subscriber is a foreign entity, provide apostilled or notarized copies of their incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all subscribers (passport or corporate registration certificate)
Power of attorney if using an agent
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or title deed)
Foreign entity incorporation documents (if applicable) with apostille
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, file an appeal with the court within 14 days or select an alternative name. If the Articles are incomplete, correct and resubmit within 7 days. For foreign documents lacking apostille, obtain the apostille from the issuing country and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증인) in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name reservation, finalize the Articles of Incorporation and have them notarized by a licensed notary public. The notary will verify the identity of all subscribers and confirm that the capital has been fully paid into a temporary bank account (if required by the notary). The notarized Articles must be signed by all subscribers or their legal representatives. If any subscriber is a corporation, the corporate seal and a resolution of its board authorizing the subscription must be attached. The notary will issue a notarial certificate, which is a mandatory attachment for the subsequent court registration. Ensure that the Articles include all mandatory clauses under the Commercial Act, including the company name, purpose, registered office, capital, and number of shares.
required_dossiers: Proof of capital payment (bank receipt or certificate)
Corporate resolution of each corporate subscriber (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies discrepancies, correct the Articles and re-execute. If capital payment is not verified, provide additional bank statements. If a corporate subscriber fails to provide a valid resolution, obtain a certified copy from its home jurisdiction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Commercial Registration Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Commercial Registration Court (상업등기소) – local district court registry where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for incorporation registration with the competent court registry. The application must be submitted within 2 weeks from the date of notarization. The court will review the Articles, notarial certificate, and all supporting documents. Upon approval, the court issues a Certificate of Incorporation (법인등기부등) and assigns a corporate registration number. The registration fee is payable at the court. After registration, the company becomes a legal entity with limited liability. The court will also register the directors and statutory officers as per the Articles. Ensure that the registered office address is accurately recorded.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fee
Consent of directors and officers to serve
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a query or suspension, respond within 10 days with additional documentation or corrections. Common issues include incomplete officer consents or address discrepancies. If the registration is rejected, appeal to the court within 14 days or file a new application after rectifying the defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (국세청) – local tax office; Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) – for cosmetics sales notification; local municipal office for business license
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of incorporation, register the company with the National Tax Service for corporate tax, VAT, and withholding tax. Obtain a business registration certificate (사업자등록증) from the local tax office. Simultaneously, file a cosmetics sales notification (화장품판매업 신고) with the MFDS or its regional office, as required under the Cosmetics Act. This notification is mandatory for any entity selling cosmetics, including online retailers. If the company will store cosmetics in a warehouse, obtain a warehouse license from the local municipality. Additionally, register for e-commerce compliance with the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) if the company will engage in online sales.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office delays registration, follow up with the assigned officer. If the MFDS notification is rejected due to incomplete product information, provide the required safety data and resubmit. If the business license is suspended, appeal to the municipal authority within 15 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) – Cosmetics Division; also the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) for e-commerce compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cosmetics Sales Notification (화장품판매업 신고) – mandatory for any entity selling cosmetics, including online retailers

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE) – Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable – The business is pure online retail of cosmetics with no manufacturing, chemical processing, or physical warehousing. No EIA is required. If the company later establishes a warehouse or distribution center, a separate environmental registration may be required under the Clean Air Conservation Act and Water Quality Conservation Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – No industrial discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation. If warehousing is added, compliance with the Waste Management Act for packaging waste and the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – The company does not operate a physical retail store or warehouse. If the company later leases a warehouse or office space, it must obtain a fire safety certificate from the National Fire Protection Agency (NFPA) and a workplace safety approval from the Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL) under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. For now, no civil defense or occupational clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic tax portal at hometax.go.kr; export customs clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) must first complete commercial registration with the court registry and obtain a certified copy of the corporate register. The company, through its statutory representative or authorized tax agent, must then file the Business Registration Application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business. This filing must be completed within 20 days from the commencement of business. Required supporting documents include the articles of incorporation, certified commercial register certificate, corporate seal certificate, lease agreement or proof of business premises, evidence of paid-in capital, and passport or foreign nationality documents for each non-resident representative. Upon satisfactory review, the NTS issues the Business Registration Certificate containing the unified 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the corporate Tax Identification Number, VAT registration number, and electronic tax invoice identifier. A foreign non-resident entity that is not incorporated in Korea but maintains a domestic business place follows the same registration procedure through a domestic tax representative; where the statute requires it, the entity may also obtain a non-resident registration number through HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide a check-the-box or elective corporate classification regime for domestic limited liability companies. A Yuhan Hoesa is a per se domestic corporation taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Tax Act, and no domestic hybrid mismatch elections are available to foreign investors in this entity form.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 for corporate businesses. A Yuhan Hoesa is required to register for VAT immediately upon commencing business regardless of projected turnover. For small individual entrepreneurs only, the simplified taxpayer regime is available where annual taxable gross supplies do not exceed KRW 80,000,000; a corporate entity is not eligible for the simplified taxpayer regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoicing is compulsory for all VAT-registered corporate taxpayers. The Yuhan Hoesa must issue e-tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-tax invoice portal for business-to-business supplies. If the entity uses integrated accounting software, issuance is performed through an NTS-certified EDI or API service provider that transmits invoice data to HomeTax at the time of issuance. The transmitted dataset is automatically validated against the counterparty Business Registration Number and taxpayer status, but South Korea does not operate a pre-clearance fiscal invoice approval or digital stamping model. For business-to-consumer beauty retail, credit card payment data is automatically reported to the NTS through licensed VAN operators, and cash receipts must be issued through the HomeTax Cash Receipt system whenever requested by the customer.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act applies when cosmetics goods are physically exported from South Korea pursuant to a valid export customs declaration, are transferred to a foreign buyer outside Korea, and the sale is concluded with a non-resident counterparty. The Yuhan Hoesa must prove the genuine cross-border nature of the supply; without such proof, the NTS will recharacterize the sale as a domestic taxable supply and assess VAT at the standard rate of 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service in the UNI-PASS system, including the unique export declaration number
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued in the name of the exporting Yuhan Hoesa
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Currency Acquisition Confirmation issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
Foreign exchange settlement records evidencing receipt of the export proceeds from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may scrutinize any zero-rated export claim and apply the additional tax and penalty provisions of the Value-Added Tax Act if the required customs, transport, and foreign exchange documentation cannot be produced. Unsupported export claims are recharacterized as domestic taxable supplies, resulting in an assessment of unpaid VAT plus statutory negligence surcharges and interest. Where fraudulent documents or deliberate concealment are found, the penalties may include increased additional tax and criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Incorrectly claimed VAT refunds are subject to retrospective clawback through reassessment; the general tax assessment period is five years for non-fraudulent underreporting and ten years for tax evasion or false documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Korea Customs Service under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a broadly open current account convertibility regime, but capital account operations are monitored by the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA). For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa engaged in online cosmetics retail, ordinary sales of beauty products into Korea via Shopify/PayPal will likely be collected as KRW through local payment gateways; where foreign consumers pay in USD/EUR, those receipts are classified as services/export proceeds and require settlement through an authorized foreign exchange bank. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation are not blocked for registered foreign-invested companies, but require corporate registration with a designated FX bank, proof of paid-in capital, audited financial statements, tax compliance, and a foreign investment repatriation notification. Companies that fail to register under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before capital injection may face enforcement penalties and be unable to receive foreign currency or later transfer assets abroad. The KRW is not fully internationally convertible outside the banking system and offshore trading of KRW deposits is limited to certain financial centers; however, trading between domestic resident and nonresident businesses is permissible with underlying trade and finance evidence. At present, surrender requirements do not include mandatory conversion; exporters may maintain their foreign currency proceeds for a statutory period.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters subject to FETA must collect export proceeds in foreign currency through an authorized foreign exchange bank. For goods, the standard settlement period is 18 months from the export date, or as extended by the bank based on trade terms; for services, 12 months is common; if collection cannot be achieved within the allowed period, prior permission from the MOEF/BOK is required. There is currently no mandatory surrender ratio: 0% of export proceeds must be converted into KRW. The exporter may hold the proceeds in a foreign currency deposit account, converted to KRW at market rates at its option, provided each receipt is reported through the bank's electronic foreign exchange system under the appropriate export settlement purpose code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account / KRW Demand Deposit with internet banking
Capital Escrow Account and Multi-Currency Settlement Account
Trade Settlement USD/KRW Account with Foreign Investment Reporting Support
Corporate Foreign Currency Account / Operating KRW Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as primary banking rail. Offshore digital EMIs such as Payoneer, Airwallex, or Wise are not licensed banks in South Korea under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and cannot issue standard KRW IBAN-equivalent settlement accounts, act as a receiving bank for foreign investment notifications, or provide the formal trade settlement reporting required by the Bank of Korea. An unlicensed EMI can only be used as an ancillary collection channel for Shopify/PayPal sales from selected foreign countries, with the EMI account usually being a segregated e-money account outside Korean jurisdiction. Any KRW clearing would have to pass through a licensed domestic bank, which negates the cost savings and still requires this entity to onboard at a Tier-1 bank. The FSC treats unlicensed cross-border payment service providers as prohibited banking-like activities; therefore the treasury blueprint must route all statutory capital and trade flows through licensed FX banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean Tier-1 banks will not permit a fully non-face-to-face corporate account opening for a foreign-held Yuhan Hoesa. The statutory director or an appointed officer with a notarized and apostilled limited Power of Attorney must appear physically at a Korean branch for the mandatory KYC interview. Some banks may accept a consular proxy opening in which a local attorney or certified public accountant attends the branch with an original authority document, but documentary activation of the foreign currency component usually still requires a video-call or in-person verification of the ultimate beneficial owner. After onboarding, additional security requirements include corporate wallet whitelisting, two-factor authentication, and a commitment to supply beneficial ownership updates within 14 days of any shareholder change.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign direct ownership opacity: the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident entity/individual and the shareholding chain cannot be validated quickly; any nominee or trust arrangement is treated as a red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide Certificate of Incorporation, memorandum and articles of association with full share register, shareholders' agreements, a notarized beneficial ownership certificate containing all owners above 25%, certified passports or national ID of each UBO, current corporate registry extract apostilled, certificate of good standing from the foreign domicile registry, and a sworn declaration that no nominee, bare trust, or discretionary trust holds Korean shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce revenue mismatch: the company is a low-capital cosmetics DTC retailer using Shopify/PayPal, generating high-frequency small-value transactions, refunds, and chargebacks that may be perceived as layering or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Shopify and PayPal merchant agreements, six months of settlement and chargeback statements, platform XML/CSV transaction logs, logistics and customs clearance contracts, supplier invoices and purchase orders, product catalog and pricing model, refund and return policy, prior VAT returns, and a signed explanation of the expected monthly turnover when capital is first injected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory director not resident in Korea with broad delegated powers; the bank suspects an 'office-in-a-box' or nominee director may have no real control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a board resolution specifically naming the account signatories and limiting powers of attorney to banking matters, notarized and apostilled power of attorney, proof of the director's identity and address, the local finance representative's certificate of business registration, and if acceptable to the bank, a notarized proxy letter authorizing a local CPA to attend the branch interview physically. Avoid discretionary or open-ended POA language.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cosmetics goods compliance and counterfeiting/re-exportation risk: the business may deal with ingredients banned by the Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety or with suppliers from jurisdictions subject to sanctions, causing the bank to place enhanced scrutiny on trade payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compile the MFDS cosmetic import/registration certificate or exemption letter, product safety test reports (e.g., EU CPNP, US FDA/VHL, ISO 22716 GMP), origin certificates from suppliers, no-sanctions declaration, list of raw material sources, sales channel and destination country report, and a documented export compliance policy expressing refusal to trade with sanctioned parties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Before receiving any equity injection from overseas, the foreign investor must file a foreign investment notification with KOTRA or the designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and obtain a certificate of foreign investment notification. The inbound remittance is a SWIFT MT103 where the ordering customer is the investor, the beneficiary is Yuhan Hoesa, and the reference narrative clearly states 'equity contribution capital injection' together with the foreign investment notification number and the bank's purpose code. The funds must first land in a restricted foreign-currency account, then be converted at market rate into KRW only after the FX bank verifies the notification certificate, the share subscription/contribution agreement, the paid-in capital ledger, and, where requested, an independent CPA capital contribution opinion. The bank then completes the capital transaction reporting to the Bank of Korea and issues a Foreign Exchange Remittance Remaining Report (foreign-investment proceeds reporting) used later for dividend repatriation and liquidation transfers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use standard bank-intermediated clearing rails only. For high-value or a contractually required path, open an irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) with an authorized bank for imports of cosmetics raw materials; documentary collections with draft/DA terms are acceptable for repeated, low-risk shipments from long-standing suppliers. For intangible payments such as brand licensing, software subscriptions, or marketing services, use a SWIFT MT103 denominated in the contracted currency and support the payment with the relevant service agreement and Korean withholding tax certificate. Every outbound payment must include the BOK foreign exchange transaction purpose code matching the nature of the transaction, and the bank will need the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS import declaration for physical goods and an electronic tax invoice where applicable. Settlement in cryptocurrency or via peer-to-peer platforms is prohibited by the Treasury blueprint and will be grounds for immediate account termination.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts traded with an authorized foreign exchange bank, fully covered by documented trade receivables, inventory purchases, or equity exposures in USD/EUR/JPY and matched to the future cash collection dates.

Currency swaps with a licensed Korean bank to hedge long-term cross-currency funding where the company has borrowed from a non-Korean affiliate and requires quarterly interest and principal conversion.
Plain vanilla FX options (call or put) on USD/KRW with an underlying real trade transaction and a bank-approved short-term hedging policy; no option writing strategies are permitted for this LLC.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not a permissible primary hedge for onshore Korean residents; such contracts are accepted only if the bank confirms the transaction qualifies as documented trade-related hedging and the hedge does not create leverage beyond 100% of the underlying exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Payable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for December 31 fiscal year end, due on March 31 (one-month extension available)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% additional tax for non-filing, 10% for under-reporting, daily overdue interest at 0.022% per day; after 6 months asset seizure and a court order of dissolution for chronic non-filing; criminal penalty up to 20 million KRW or 2 years imprisonment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment (Local Surtax on Corporate Income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the head office (City/Province) through WeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; for December 31 fiscal year end, due on April 30 (one-month extension available with the national return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% additional tax for non-filing, 10% for under-reporting, daily overdue interest at 0.022% per day, enforced collection and refusal to issue tax clearance certificate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements (for companies exceeding audit thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (attached to corporate tax return) and the Financial Supervisory Service/Securities & Futures Commission when required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and the auditor's report finalized before the annual members general meeting, which must occur within 3 months after fiscal year-end; audited financial statements must be filed with the corporate tax return by March 31 for a December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a statutory auditor triggers administrative fine up to 10 million KRW; late submission to FSS incurs additional fines; audited statements are void for tax purposes and may result in criminal liability for the auditor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Foreign Investment Enterprise (if foreign equity is 100 million KRW or more)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via KOTRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the end of each fiscal year (for a December year-end, due by January 15)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to 5 million KRW and loss of foreign-invested company rights for the following year

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) is legally required to appoint a statutory external auditor under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies when total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed 12 billion KRW (approximately USD 9.0 million at 1,330 KRW/USD). An audit is also mandatory if the company is listed, if it was previously audited and continues to meet the threshold, or if it is designated by the Securities and Futures Commission under the Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for externally audited companies; non-listed companies with total assets below 12 billion KRW may apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Standards) issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board. All statutory audits are performed under Korean Auditing Standards (KAS).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Korean Commercial Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a Yuhan Hoesa must maintain an internal register of members and must update beneficial ownership details within 30 days of any transfer of membership interests. There is no separate public annual UBO return; however, for foreign-invested companies with foreign shareholding above 100 million KRW, the ultimate beneficial owner must be confirmed in the annual KOTRA report, and material ownership changes must be reported in the annual corporate tax return's shareholder information supplement.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Director Myeongbu) with service contracts
Register of Registered Pledges and Usufructs on Membership Interests
Minutes of Members General Meetings (Sawon Chonghoe Minutes)
Statutory Accounting Books and Financial Statements (ledgers, journals, inventory records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 2,500 per year (typical South Korean corporate secretary and registered address service provider fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 35,000 for a mandatory statutory audit; USD 1,500 – USD 5,000 for a voluntary review of a below-threshold small LLC

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% federal top marginal corporate income tax rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion, plus a 10% local corporate income tax surcharge on the federal corporate tax, producing a 23.1% aggregate headline effective rate before treaty and incentive adjustments
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general offshore or free-zone income tax holiday applies to an online cosmetics beauty retail business operating through a Korean Yuhan Hoesa. Available incentives include the small and medium enterprise preferential corporate tax rate of 9% on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income, the R&D tax credit under the Special Tax Limitation Control Act, employment tax credits, and foreign-investment-related reductions for qualifying high-technology or foreign-investment zone facilities. Standard online beauty retail sales income is fully taxable after normal deductions; no patent-box regime applies unless the entity has qualifying registered Korean IP with transferable royalty rights.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return known as Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal; the filing package includes the principal declaration form, financial statement reconciliation schedules, Schedule of International Transactions, transfer pricing disclosures, and the non-resident withholding reconciliation attachments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end the filing deadline is March 31 of the following year. A foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa may apply for an extension under the Corporate Tax Act but must still make provisional tax payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, corporate name, head office address, fiscal year end, business classification code, industry code, representative director, and shareholder identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean business registration number for the Yuhan Hoesa. If the filing is made for a Korean permanent establishment of a foreign parent, mark the non-resident corporation box and attach the parent authority's registration details. Use ISIC 4791 / NAICS 456120 for online retail of cosmetics and personal care products. Any direct online sales generated by the Korean entity must be disclosed as Korean-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Reconciliation of Book Income to Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book net income before tax is adjusted for non-deductible items, tax-exempt income, temporary differences, reserves, and provisions recognized under the Korean tax reconciliation schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean-resident Yuhan Hoesa, include all world-wide income properly statemented in Korea. For a non-resident filing through a Korean PE, include only Korean-source income attributable to the PE under the arm's length principle. Add back non-deductible intercompany management fees lacking economic substance, entertainment expenses above statutory limits, and unsubstantiated beauty freemium marketing costs. Remove foreign-source e-commerce revenue only where the DTA assigns taxing rights exclusively outside Korea and there is no Korean solicitation activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tax Base and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute final taxable income after applying tax-exempt measures, special deductions, and unabsorbed tax loss carryforwards within the statutory carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 5-year net operating loss carryforward limit strictly. Do not deduct losses from a foreign parent or overseas branch unless the relevant income is subject to Korean tax under the applicable DTA. The Yuhan Hoesa must attach a Schedule of Loss Carryforward showing year of loss, original loss amount, offset year, and remaining balance; losses cannot reduce profits attributable to a non-resident shareholder prior to corporate income tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Final Corporate Income Tax Calculation and Local Surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive corporate tax rate schedule to the taxable base, compute federal corporate income tax, and compute the 10% local corporate income tax surcharge on the federal tax amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident Yuhan Hoesa taxable through a Korean PE is taxed on the PE taxable base at the same progressive rates as a domestic corporation. No deemed distribution or tax-free pass-through election is allowed; the entity is entity-level taxed. If the entity is a limited liability constrained as a Korean Yuhan Hoesa, corporate profits are subject to Korean corporate tax before any dividend withholding on actual remittance to foreign owners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Foreign Tax Credit and Special Tax Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter foreign income taxes paid on foreign-source income, R&D credits, employment expansion credits, and other allowable deductions under the Special Tax Limitation Control Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A domestic Korean Yuhan Hoesa may claim foreign tax credits for foreign withholding taxes on cross-border online sales if the related foreign income is included in Korean taxable income. A non-resident PE cannot credit taxes paid by its foreign head office on Korean-source income unless a specific DTA provision grants such credit. Cosmetic retail e-commerce through foreign marketplaces must document the exact foreign sales and taxes paid to avoid double counting or erroneous treaty credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Schedule of International Transactions and Transfer Pricing Disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all cross-border related-party transactions including purchases of finished beauty products, raw cosmetic ingredients, trademark royalties, software and marketplace app license fees, website maintenance fees, technical services, marketing group charges, and intercompany financing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Report on International Transactions where the statutory threshold is met. Select the OECD-compliant arm's length method best suited to the function of the Korean beauty retail entity: for wholesale distribution of cosmetics, transactional net margin method or resale price method; for licensing of trademarks in Korea, comparable uncontrolled price or profit split method. The Korean tax authorities can reject a foreign entity's transactions that are not supported by contemporaneous local file and master file documentation. Missing TD schedules may result in a 30% accuracy penalty on underreported tax and separate information return penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Withholding Tax Reconciliation on Non-Resident Profit Repatriation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare dividends declared and paid, interest paid, royalties paid, rentals, and amounts distributable to non-resident shareholders, foreign lenders, and foreign intellectual property owners during the tax year, including domestic withholding tax and local surcharge computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Yuhan Hoesa as payer must withhold 20% national tax plus 2% local surcharge on gross dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents, unless a DTA provides a reduced rate. For each treaty-based payment, attach the Beneficial Ownership Statement, the foreign Tax Residency Certificate, proof that the non-resident has no Korean PE to which the income is effectively connected, and evidence of actual ownership and entitlement. Dividends paid to a foreign shareholder cannot be deducted in computing Box 4 corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Economic Substance, Treaty Protection, and Anti-Abuse Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirm that the Korean entity has real presence, decision-making, employees, bank accounts, and operational substance, and that any treaty intermediary has genuine principal purpose and beneficial ownership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean tax authority applies the substance-over-form principle and, for relevant treaty partners, the Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test. The Yuhan Hoesa must demonstrate that its management decisions, purchase orders, inventory risk assumption, customer contracts, payment processing systems and after-sales service are actively performed in Korea. If a foreign holding or IP vehicle lacks core income-generating activities, treaty benefits are denied, the company is recharacterized as a Peppercorn shell, and all prior underwithholding is assessed with interest and penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return subjects the taxpayer to an unfiled-return penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; an understated-return accuracy penalty of 10% for negligent understatement and up to 40% for intentional concealment; plus monthly collection interest computed from the statutory due date until payment. Failure to file the Schedule of International Transactions can trigger separate information return penalties and transfer pricing accuracy penalties. Where tax evasion is identified, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may impose imprisonment or fines equal to a multiple of the evaded tax, and the responsible director can be listed in the departure prohibition system and his personal assets pursued.
